extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners and individuals petitioning for reinstatement before the USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Petitioning for reinstatement to practice before the United States Patent and Trademark Office under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58; the Office of Enrollment and Discipline reviews the petition, supporting affidavit, and the record to determine whether reinstatement is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit pursuant to 37 CFR § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr. Chow filed an Affidavit pursuant to 37 CFR § 11.58 in support of the Petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition for reinstatement should be supported by an affidavit filed in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58. (The decision document cites the filing requirement but does not reproduce the substantive contents required by the regulation.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Record-based review of petitioner's eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: After careful review of the Petition, the supporting affidavit, and all information in the record material to his eligibility for reinstatement, the Director ... determined that reinstatement ... is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director's decision is based on a comprehensive review of the petition, the supporting affidavit, and all record information material to eligibility. Petitioners should ensure their petition and affidavit, and any record evidence, address all matters relevant to eligibility for reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's discretionary determination of 'appropriateness' for reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the Office of Enrollment and Discipline determined that reinstatement of Mr. Chow to practice before the United States Patent and Trademark Office is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement is granted when the Director, exercising discretion, finds reinstatement to be 'appropriate' based on the materials reviewed. The decision document indicates the outcome turns on the Director's assessment rather than a single enumerated checklist; specifics of the standard of appropriateness are not detailed in this order.
